lens_summary: External data for training, checked against the repo and the web on 25 Sep. (1) The only same-instrument, same-scale public recording is the Ultrack 'dorado' movie. It is the 44b6 embryo itself (tools/register_44b6_dorado.py), so it adds label DENSITY (458,519 Ultrack tracks with links, tools/dorado_crops.py) and ~5x more space-time of that embryo. It adds NO embryo diversity, and embryo shift is what sinks transfer: a 6bba-only scratch model scores 0.68 on 44b6 against 0.88 for the all-199 public model (experiments/RESULTS.md rows 80-81). The ultrack_supplementary repo shows this movie was tracked by the 'sparse_zebrafish' pipeline (DS_LENGTH 521, UNet weights unet-simview.pt; SimView is the multi-view design the hosts describe). The hosts' GT is proofread Ultrack: N_est is about 0.91 x the Ultrack count, and Ultrack sits a median 1.29 um from GT (research/wf_ideas_v2/r2_research_dorado-oos-lab.json). (2) The team has used external data only once: a dorado DaughterNet, closed at val AUC 0.62. Nobody has trained a DETECTOR on external dense labels. The planned dense fine-tune used SELF-teacher labels (no new information) and was cancelled before it ran (CONTEXT.md 473-495, 1005). So the detector line is untested, not closed. (3) Key new structural fact: in the x138 stack BIOHUB_SECONDARY_DETECTION_WEIGHT=0.80. The SECONDARY model provides 80% of the detection logits, while the V1284 head and the main edge net read only PRIMARY features. A dense-label SECONDARY therefore changes where nodes are without breaking the head. The lever is strong both ways: three sparse secondary swaps scored -0.016/-0.025/-0.007 on the LB (RESULTS.md lines 39, 42, 46). (4) Multiplier trap: in the lab, exp39's node ratio is 44b6 -0.164, 6bba -0.021 (GT-edge-weighted, l5_per_video_confirmation_vs_exp39.csv). A detector that imitates dense Ultrack (~1.1 N_est) would lose ~2.6% / ~1.2% of adj_edge through the node factor, so every dense model must be threshold-recalibrated to the baseline N_pred. (5) Other sources are weak for 4 days. Zebrahub single-objective ZSNS001-005 (DaXi, 1.24 x 0.439 x 0.439 um, a different optical design; tracks unverified) and CTC 3D nuclei sets (other organisms) are domain-shifted. FOCUS-3D/StarDist-type public detectors have no LB proof (hengck23). The Freitas synthetic set is closed. A head retrain on dorado pairs is dominated by the 44b6->6bba kill-test result: 44b6-trained head 1.5699 um vs public 1.5668 um (coordhead_retrain/out_full_P.log). It learns the 44b6 convention. HONEST CEILING OF THE LENS: only a detector-level change can reach >= +0.005. In the in-sample lab, fixing 25% of the detection + swap FN (5,104 of 6,732) at constant N_pred gives about +0.009 adj_edge. Model-ranking transfer to the LB is poor (hikaggler r ~ -0.2; our fine-tunes 0.944/0.943 vs 0.947). Realistic expectation for the best idea: ~0 +- 0.008 public, P(>= +0.005) about 10-15%. 0.99 is unreachable under this lens, and under any lens before 29 Sep: it would need adj_edge ~0.95 plus div_J ~0.4. The lens is worth one or two probes because it is the only route the top teams (Tang: 'most gains from model improvements') say worked.

hypotheses.title: Fine-tune the x138 SECONDARY detector (80% of detection logits) on dorado dense Ultrack pseudo-tracks mixed with Kaggle sparse GT; primary, V1284 head and tail untouched
hypotheses.mechanism: The loss is a density problem: in the densest 6bba quartile 52% of the loss comes from 37% swap and 29% never-detected FN (BRIEF; research/wf_ideas_v2/r2_critic.json). The public detectors were trained with ONE positive voxel per annotated nucleus. Every other voxel, including the 85-99% of nuclei that are not annotated, is a weak negative (tools/repo/scripts/train_unet_transformer.py:535, neg weight 0.01). So the model never received positive supervision in exactly the dense regions where it fails. The dorado Ultrack tracks label every nucleus with links, in the host annotation convention (GT = proofread Ultrack; N_est ~0.91 x Ultrack count). In x138 the secondary supplies 80% of the detection logits (SECONDARY_DETECTION_WEIGHT 0.80) while the V1284 head and the main edge net read the primary's features. So a dense-trained secondary changes node existence and placement without invalidating the head that gave x138 its +0.007.
hypotheses.change: (1) Agent writes tools/dorado_clips.py, reusing the tools/dorado_crops.py streaming and tools/build_dense_gt.py geff writer. From dorado level 0 it cuts Kaggle-format clips (zarr 1x64x256x256 per frame, uint16, image_statistics quantiles 0.001/0.999 computed like the Kaggle clips, geff with all Ultrack points in the box plus their track edges, divisions kept, estimated_number_of_nodes = 0.91 x points). Clips are 20 frames long, over 3 time blocks x 2 z-chunks, keeping boxes whose Ultrack density is within the Kaggle 160-734 points/frame range: ~150 clips, about 3-4 GB compressed. Boxes overlapping placed 44b6 clips are allowed for training (the test is other embryos). One late block (t 380-420, z0 64, the 16 boxes free of 44b6 in r2_research_dorado-oos-lab.json) is HELD OUT. (2) The user runs it on Colab (public.czbiohub.org is reachable there, not from the container) and uploads it as a private Kaggle dataset with the Kaggle API token. (3) Kaggle GPU kernel: train_unet_transformer.py --init-weights <seed314159 secondary>, joint UNet+transformer (no freeze), data = competition train (199 sparse) + dorado clips at 1:1 window sampling, lr 3e-5, 1200-2000 iterations, bce, det_neg_weight 0.01. (4) Recalibrate: pick the secondary's detection threshold/alignment so the blended N_pred on 20 6bba lab videos stays within +-2% of the x138 baseline. (5) New build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 patch 'secondary': overrides BIOHUB_SECONDARY_WEIGHTS. The DEFAULT probe variant AVERAGES the aligned logits of seed314159 and the dense model inside the 0.8 secondary slot (variance control), and the full swap is the second variant. Everything else stays byte-identical to exp56/exp57b.

hypotheses.upper_bound: Lab (in-sample) J = 122,151/(122,151+6,846+6,732) = 0.900. Detection+swap FN = a_* 2,929 + b_swap 2,175 = 5,104 (fn_anatomy_exp39.md). Fixing 25% of them at constant N_pred and FP: +1,276 TP -> J 0.9094 = +0.0094. With the secondary only at weight 0.8 (averaged variant: 0.4), take ~60% of that: about +0.006. Hard cap if every detection+swap FN were fixed: +0.038. Node factor: every +1% N_pred costs ~0.0009 adj.
hypotheses.expected_public_gain: -0.004 .. +0.006 (central ~+0.001). Arithmetic: 25% capture scenario +0.006 x P(transfer ~0.35) minus a harm tail (3/3 earlier secondary swaps negative, mean -0.016; with the averaged variant and N_pred recalibration, assume a 30% chance of about -0.004).
hypotheses.expected_private_gain: Similar to public, with slightly higher variance. Private is ~71% other embryos, and the dense labels come from the 44b6 embryo only (no embryo diversity).
hypotheses.probability: P(LB >= base + 0.005) ~10%; P(>= +0.002) ~25%; P(<= -0.003) ~30%. Reasoning: a genuinely new label source on the strongest detection lever, but every model swap so far has been negative on the LB, and dorado adds density, not a new embryo.
hypotheses.validation_protocol: PRE-REGISTERED, before any LB slot. (a) PARITY: a dorado box cut at a registered 44b6 placement (kaggle44b6_in_dorado.json) must reproduce that Kaggle clip: pixel Pearson r >= 0.99, and quantiles within 2%. Otherwise the normalisation differs: stop. (b) OOS KILL GATE on the held-out dorado block (t 380-420, 16 boxes never inside any 44b6 clip, unseen by the public models and excluded from fine-tuning). Run the full x138 prediction stage (raw ILP graph) with the base vs the new secondary. Score recall of Ultrack points at 7 um and at 3 um at matched N_pred (+-2%), plus edge-J vs the Ultrack pseudo-tracks cut at divisions. Gate: 7-um recall +1.0 pp or more AND pseudo edge-J +0.005 or more, with >= 11/16 boxes non-negative. Distances are not gated (convention bias, 1.29 um pseudo-GT noise). (c) IN-SAMPLE SANITY on 20 6bba lab videos with the official metric: the public models saw these videos, so the check is biased AGAINST the new model. It must not lose more than 0.005 adj_edge and must keep N_pred within 2%. (d) Only then one LB probe vs exp56/exp57b (same base, one change). Promotion needs LB >= base + 0.003 (LB noise ~0.003).

hypotheses.title: Rider: in-kernel unet-simview (public pretrained SimView UNet) foreground/centroid candidates added to x138's READMIT / gap-filler candidate pool (no model of ours changes)
hypotheses.mechanism: x138's readmit and gap filler can only add nodes from the primary's own sub-threshold peaks (lowdet >= 0.3). About 31% of FN involve a node the detector never produced (BRIEF), in 44b6 mostly under-segmentation where Ultrack has ~44% more interior points (r2_critic.json). A domain-matched external detector supplies candidates exactly where the primary merged two nuclei. The readmit gates (within 4 um of an open track end/start, > 2 um from any node, <= 3% added nodes) keep the node factor small. Because the candidate source is external, lab gains are less in-sample than network-confidence rules.
hypotheses.change: Upload unet-simview.pt as a private dataset. In the x138 predict patch, run it once per frame (torchscript, fp16, with (1,2,2) downsampling if runtime requires it) and take centroids of foreground components split by boundary-map maxima (simple watershed). Append them to _LOWDET with a score of 0.97 so they pass READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.965. Gap filler: allow them as 'free sub-threshold peaks'. New patch 'simview' in build_probe_kernel --base x138, exact no-op when off.
